scenario: AITA for not hosting thanksgiving like I planned to | For about 50 years, my mom hosted all of her children and grandchildren for thanksgiving and Christmas Eve. She’s now gotten too old and asked us kids to take over the tradition. There are 4 of us so we just rotate. We’ve each hosted one holiday so far. This thanksgiving is my turn. We have never spent thanksgiving or Christmas Eve with my wife’s family. We’ve just never been as close to them plus they live all over the country. Well this year her mom and aunts decided to go to the Macy’s thanksgiving day parade. At first it was just a sister’s trip but then they decided to invite all their kids and grandkids to meet them up there. My wife really wants to go. She hasnt seen some of her aunts and cousins in years. Our daughter wants to go because it’s a “once in a lifetime event” (which i agree with). And I want to go. As soon as we decided to go I called my older brother to see what we should do about thanksgiving because I can’t host this year. He said our oldest sister is going to be pissed and i have to tell her myself. He wished me luck. So I call her and she is mad. She says she’ll probably have to end up hosting even though she is up next for Christmas and I’m being inconsiderate of what our mom asked us to do. “Mom wouldn’t abandon thanksgiving to go to nyc” and went on about how sad mom will be that I’m doing this. I offered to pay for them to rent a spot and have it catered but she said that takes away from the close knit family vibe. My brother said his wife might be up for it but he didn’t sound too happy about asking her. My other sister can’t do it because she’s renovating her house. I do feel bad for backing out of my turn but I tried to offer up solutions and I also offered to host the next holiday—which my oldest sister said no to because it’s her turn and she’s been planning for it all year. Next up is my brother so I said me and him could maybe just swap thanksgivings if his wife is up for it. Am I in the wrong here?

However, its importance justifies its inclusion, though efficiency could be considered. 3. **Balancing Tradition and Time**: To respect both tradition and time constraints, the ceremony could be streamlined. This might involve grouping elders, having representatives, or setting up multiple serving stations to reduce duration without losing meaning. 4. **Couple's Preferences**: The couple's values and wishes are paramount. If they prioritize tradition, maintaining the ceremony as is is appropriate. If modernization is desired, a shorter, symbolic version could suffice. 5. **Guest Experience**: Ensuring guests understand the ceremony's significance can enhance their patience. Engaging elements like music or speeches might make the time more enjoyable. In conclusion, while respecting the tradition is crucial, finding a balance through efficiency and engagement can make the ceremony meaningful without excessive length. The couple's preferences and the cultural context should guide the decision.

Each of us has hosted one holiday so far. This year, it's my turn to host Thanksgiving. But here's the thing: my wife's family isn't as close, and they live all over the country. We've never spent Thanksgiving or Christmas Eve with them. However, this year, her mom and aunts decided to go to the Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade. Initially, it was just a sister's trip, but then they invited all their kids and grandkids to meet up there. My wife really wants to go because she hasn't seen some of her aunts and cousins in years. Our daughter also wants to go because she thinks it's a "once in a lifetime event," and I agree with that. Plus, I want to go too. So, as soon as we decided to go, I called my older brother to see what we should do about Thanksgiving since I can't host this year. He said our oldest sister is going to be pissed and that I have to tell her myself. He wished me luck. So I called her, and she was mad. She said she'll probably have to end up hosting even though she's up next for Christmas, and I'm being inconsiderate of what our mom asked us to do.
